subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should this five-PR durable-core stack land in order on release/2026.7.1, be retargeted to current main, or be deferred to a later release?
rationale: The branch adds shared persisted state, Gateway contracts, plugin SDK surface, and startup recovery behavior to a release line that is already published; code review cannot choose that release and sequencing policy safely.

options.title: Land ordered stack after proof
options.body: Keep the release target, land the predecessor PRs first, and require exact-head fresh-enable, upgrade, reset, and restart evidence before this final slice.

options.title: Retarget the stack to main
options.body: Rebase the full stack onto current main and repeat compatibility and real-runtime proof against the resulting heads before review.

options.title: Defer durable core
options.body: Pause or close the release-line stack and revisit the capability in a later planned release with a maintainer-owned rollout.

recommendation.title: Land ordered stack after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the release target, land the predecessor PRs first, and require exact-head fresh-enable, upgrade, reset, and restart evidence before this final slice.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the durable session-delivery queue and startup recovery boundary most directly affected by the release decision.
